title: Marginal savings per GPU hire-swap heuristic — Oct 2026
body:
Executive summary:
This is a working spreadsheet-style analysis to evaluate a simple heuristic: when does hiring (or redeploying) engineering capacity to operate, optimize, and consolidate GPU infrastructure pay for itself relative to buying or leasing additional GPU capacity? The goal is to produce an actionable, quick-to-read rule-of-thumb the GTM/ops and finance teams can use when negotiating capacity vs hiring tradeoffs.

Quick take:
- One fully-burdened ML/infra engineer (FTE) at our assumed rate (~$18k/mo) is cost-neutral if they can eliminate or shift ~10 reserved GPUs into a cheaper mode (spot/lease or consolidation) that saves ~$1.8k/GPU/mo.
- If an engineer enables quantization/stack optimizations that reduce effective GPU need by >=15 GPUs, that is strongly accretive (~$27k+ net savings/mo).
- Practical recommended threshold: commit to hiring only if expected sustained GPU delta managed >=12 GPUs per FTE (buffered for ramp and risk).

Assumptions (basecase — adjust per customer/region):
- Fully-burdened engineer monthly cost (salary + benefits + overhead): $18,000/mo
- Reserved dedicated GPU unit cost (monthly effective): $3,600/GPU/mo
- Spot/lease fallback GPU unit cost: $1,800/GPU/mo
- Operational consolidation (via batching, model pruning, caching): per-GPU effective demand reduction possible, varies by workload (we test +10%, +15%, +25%)
- One FTE can realistically drive consolidation + tooling for N GPUs/month (N modeled below)
- Time horizon for ROI: 3 months to operationalize, 6–12 months to realize steady-state

Tabular scenarios (monthly totals) — baseline numbers for a single availability pool:
Scenario,Reserved GPUs,FTEs,GPU monthly cost,FTE monthly cost,Total monthly cost,Delta vs baseline,Notes
Baseline,100,10,$360,000,$180,000,$540,000,$0,Current mix (reserved-only)
Hire-swap (consolidate),80,12,$288,000,$216,000,$504,000,-$36,000,Reduce GPUs by 20% via hire-driven consolidation and add 2 FTEs for ops
Lease-fallback (mixed),70 reserved + 30 spot,10,$(70*3600+30*1800)=$324,000,$180,000,$504,000,-$36,000,Move 30 GPUs to spot lease, no headcount delta
Quantization uplift,85,11,$306,000,$198,000,$504,000,-$36,000,15% effective GPU reduction via quant + 1 extra FTE to deliver

Break-even math (simple):
- Cost saved per GPU when moved from reserved to spot = CR - CS = 3600 - 1800 = $1,800/month
- FTE monthly cost = CFTE = $18,000/month
- Break-even GPUs per FTE (G_break) = CFTE / (CR - CS) = 18000 / 1800 = 10 GPUs
Interpretation: If a single hire can convert or permanently reduce >=10 GPUs from reserved to cheaper modes (or eliminate them via optimization), the hire pays back on purely unit economics within one month (if savings are realized immediately).

Sensitivity checks (varying the per-GPU savings):
- If spot price rises to $2,400/mo (savings per GPU = 1200), G_break = 15 GPUs/FTE
- If reserved GPU cost falls to $3,000/mo (e.g., better cloud deal), savings=1200 -> G_break = 15 GPUs/FTE
- If CFTE is higher (senior hires at $25k/mo), with base savings 1800 -> G_break = 13.9 -> ~14 GPUs/FTE

Optimization impact framing (conservative vs aggressive):
- Conservative: 1 FTE drives 8–10 GPUs to spot/fall back or consolidate -> marginal or break-even (recommend short trial hires + target 12 GPUs before repeating)
- Realistic: 1 FTE executes infra and model improvements that yield 12–18 GPU-equivalents (mix of leasing and elimination) -> positive savings
- Aggressive: 1 FTE enables model-level quantization + runtime ops leading to 20+ GPU reduction -> clear net savings and headroom for reinvestment

Runway & strategic considerations:
- Hiring accelerates operational maturity (reduces incident MTTR, improves evacuation to spot for overflow). The financial rule-of-thumb should be combined with reliability/SLAs: some GPUs must remain reserved for latency-sensitive customers.
- Headcount decisions drive multi-month fixed cost; prefer staged hiring (canary 1 FTE for 6–8 weeks) and a 12-week assessment window with explicit triggers to expand.
- Pricing negotiation: using this heuristic, sales/finance can evaluate whether to offer customers a capacity discount vs expecting to fund headcount to operate bespoke capacity.

Actionable next steps (for finance, infra, product):
1) Re-run the model with per-region GPU unit rates (us-west vs eu-north) and real spot deltas — assign to Diego to produce regionized sheet (JIRA-FIN-3421).
2) Run a 12-week hire-candidate pilot: hire 1 infra FTE, target 12 GPUs consolidation, report weekly. If >=12 GPUs sustained after 12 weeks, greenlight hire-window x2. Owner: Rina (Ops).
3) Instrument quasi-automated dashboard: GPU counts by route, cost per route, FTE time allocation — tie to Redwood Console metrics (link audit). Owner: Evan (Platform).
4) Add a second dimension: quality/regression risk cost (estimated customer SLA penalty per outage) to convert purely cost-first signal into risk-adjusted decision.

Risks & caveats:
- Spot availability: moving capacity to spot/less expensive leasing carries preemption risk; some customers require reserved capacity regardless of unit economics.
- Measurement noise: attributing GPU reductions to a single hire is tricky; use controlled experiments and holdout pools.
- Hidden labor: onboarding, cross-team coordination, and escalations add to CFTE beyond pure coding hours — assume 10–20% overhead in practice.

Appendix: worked example formulas (for the sheet engine)
- GPU_monthly_cost = reserved_gpus * reserved_unit_cost + spot_gpus * spot_unit_cost
- FTE_monthly_cost = ftes * fte_unit_cost
- Total_monthly_cost = GPU_monthly_cost + FTE_monthly_cost
- Delta_vs_baseline = Total_monthly_cost - baseline_total_monthly_cost
- G_break = fte_unit_cost / (reserved_unit_cost - spot_unit_cost)

Suggested readouts for leadership slide (one pager):
- Single number rule: hire if you expect >=12 GPU-equivalent sustained reduction per FTE
- Sensitivity: show G_break across three price bands (savings/GPU = $1.2k | $1.8k | $2.4k) and FTE cost bands ($14k | $18k | $25k)
- Pilot ask: 1 FTE for 12 weeks, target 12 GPUs, snapshot baseline vs week 12 cost delta

Notes & provenance:
- Back-of-envelope unit costs pulled from vendor rate cards and internal procurement (Q3–Q4 2026 estimates).
- Connected artifacts: JIRA-FIN-3421 (regionized costing task), CONFLUENCE-PRICING-56 (capacity negotiation playbook), GH PR for cost-analysis code referenced above.

Document status: draft — intended for internal review with finance/infra/product. Request feedback on the per-GPU unit costs and an updated conservative ramp profile for FTE impact (please annotate the sheet with real measured deltas where available).
